fy3v9wrrhvdwbfw4wevnb852.heroText:
I'm **Manuel Eigen**, **Designer** & **Full-Stack Developer**.
I design brands, websites & shops – and build them myself. Design and code from a single source, for companies, agencies & culture.
fy3v9wrrhvdwbfw4wevnb852.aboutText:
For more than ten years I've been working at the intersection of design, technology & craft – for companies, agencies, NGOs and cultural projects.

I started out as a graphic designer, trained at Lette Verein Berlin. Then UX/UI came along, and more and more code – until I wanted to build the products myself that I had only designed before. After further training as a JavaScript Full-Stack Developer, that's exactly what I do today: I design brands, websites & shops and develop them too.

I work in a structured way, say early when something isn't working, and stay curious – about new tools as much as about your topic. Whether it's a Shopware shop or a festival app: I bring ideas to the point visually and build solutions that are well thought out and stay accessible.

For you, that means one point of contact from the first sketch to launch – with nothing lost in the handover between design and development.

ry63l39k813qw3cz7imt93xe.title: Branding & Corporate Identity
ry63l39k813qw3cz7imt93xe.description:
Your brand should be recognized – on a business card as much as in the shop and on social media? Then it needs a system, not just a logo.
I develop visual identities that show attitude and can be applied consistently. From logo, typography and color system to implementation in print, web and physical space: I think of brands as modular, cross-media systems, with a clear view of users and context.

### Services:
- Brand strategy & visual guidelines
- Logo development & design systems
- Corporate manuals & templates
- Brand rollout for print, web & social
ry63l39k813qw3cz7imt93xe.teaser: Visual identities that show attitude – from logo to design system.

ghrryo09wi3uxj68ucu2d22m.title: 3D Design & Visualization
ghrryo09wi3uxj68ucu2d22m.description:
I build digital spaces, products and images that make an impact.
Using Cinema 4D and the Corona Renderer, I create photorealistic renderings, motion graphics or interactive 3D experiences. Especially for products, I combine my design expertise with technical precision.

### Services:
- 3D modeling & visualization
- Product animation & motion design
- Architectural & spatial visualizations
- 3D assets for web, print, social & AR

bnanr6fstd07ho43w1igja8l.title: Web Design, Development & E-Commerce
bnanr6fstd07ho43w1igja8l.description:
Your website or shop should look good, load fast and be easy to maintain later without an agency? Then you need someone who thinks design and technology together – and is still around after launch.
I design and develop websites and shops from the first wireframe to going live – as a designer who writes the code himself. My focus is on modular, maintainable solutions: headless setups with Next.js & Strapi, classic WordPress sites, web apps that also run offline, or online shops with Shopware & Shopify. For five years I designed, developed and step by step extended the Shopware shop of Oberflächenwelt: theme, interface, custom features in PHP & Twig. That's exactly the mix I offer – design and code from a single source, always with a heart for usability.

### Services:
- UI/UX concept & design – for websites and shops
- Web development with React, Next.js, TypeScript & Tailwind
- CMS solutions: Strapi, WordPress
- Shopware 6 & Shopify: setup, theme development, plugins
- Redesign & migration of existing shops
- Accessibility (WCAG), performance, SEO & responsive design
- Maintenance & further development after launch
bnanr6fstd07ho43w1igja8l.teaser: Websites & shops that load fast, look good and can be maintained without an agency.

f9qgwffymxyfo226nph9clzc.title: Editorial & Print Design
f9qgwffymxyfo226nph9clzc.description:
You have content that should be read – in print or as a PDF? Then structure, typography and imagery have to work together, or the best parts get lost.
I design print products with a feel for content and high design standards. Whether magazine, brochure or handbook: my focus is on functional design that communicates content clearly and is aesthetically convincing at the same time – right through to the final print file.

### Services:
- Layout & design for magazines, catalogs, brochures
- Typography & imagery concepts, infographics & pictograms
- Grid systems & page architecture
- Print preparation, production support & accessible PDFs

bodypage.Text: Pickawood sells made-to-measure furniture online – shelves, cabinets and tables that customers configure themselves. The heart of the shop is the furniture configurator: dimensions, material and layout can be adjusted down to the millimeter without losing track. I designed the configurator's interface and key shop flows and visualized the furniture in 3D – for the configurator, the shop and the printed catalogs. That makes the flexibility of the products visible before anyone orders.

bodypage.Text: Oberflächenwelt is a Berlin-based specialist wholesaler for mineral paints and fine plasters – high-quality surfaces for architecture and design projects. For more than five years I designed and technically developed the Shopware-based online shop: from the theme and the interface to custom shop features in PHP, Symfony and Twig. On top of that came 3D visualizations of the products and ongoing maintenance. Design and development from a single source – exactly the combination I offer today as a Designer & Full-Stack Developer.

Tech: Shopware 6 with a custom theme (Twig, SCSS, JavaScript) – custom shop features as plugins in PHP & Symfony – local development with Docker, version control with Git – product visualizations in Cinema 4D.

cr6ei21lcqi8lf5r2tb1m2q9.title: Diakonie Handbook: Young Carers

bodypage.Text: Commissioned by EPYC and Diakonisches Werk Berlin Stadtmitte, I designed the 76-page handbook “Empowering Professionals to Support Young Carers”. It is built on a precise two-column grid with clear typographic hierarchies and subtle color coding that guides professionals through background knowledge, practical guides and modular working materials. I was responsible for the entire editorial design: layout concept, infographics, pictogram set, image research, typesetting, and the output as print-optimized and accessible PDF versions.

cr6ei21lcqi8lf5r2tb1m2q9.role: Editorial design, infographics & accessible PDF output

bodypage.Text: For the entropie festival I conceived, designed and developed the digital festival guide: a Progressive Web App built on Next.js and Strapi that brings together the program, acts and info – and thanks to its offline mode keeps working even when the network drops out on the festival grounds. The festival team maintains the content themselves in the CMS. From the first wireframes through the UI to deployment on Vercel, everything came from a single source.

Tech: frontend with Next.js (React), installable as a Progressive Web App – offline mode so the program & info stay available without a network – backend with Strapi as headless CMS, content maintained by the festival team – hosting & deployment on Vercel, version control with Git.

mdwmtudwb8egdh4d0xrv08gq.question: What exactly do you do – design or development?
mdwmtudwb8egdh4d0xrv08gq.answer: Both, and deliberately so. I started out as a graphic designer and picked up more and more code over the years – by now with a degree as a Full-Stack Developer. For you, that means: you get your brand, website or shop from a single source, with nothing lost between concept and implementation. If a project only needs design or only development, that works just as well.

mxeg0w5kmrcw0w1e95kvh16j.question: What does working together cost?
mxeg0w5kmrcw0w1e95kvh16j.answer: That depends on the scope, so you'll get a concrete quote after an initial conversation. As a guide: my day rate is €600 net. Smaller projects like a logo or a brochure start at around €800–1,500 net; complete brand identities or websites including development usually range between €3,000 and €10,000 net. I'm happy to quote clearly defined projects at a fixed price; ongoing collaboration is billed by time and effort.

w0murdgrcwwrrg91isaa3ua7.question: What kinds of projects do you take on?
w0murdgrcwwrrg91isaa3ua7.answer: Brand identities from logo to corporate design, editorial & print, websites and web apps, online shops with Shopware or Shopify. My clients are companies, agencies, cultural institutions, NGOs and start-ups – ranging from a theater campaign to an e-commerce platform.

u0qaybnz1ce5lyg1brrkdln9.question: What software and tools do you use for your design projects?
u0qaybnz1ce5lyg1brrkdln9.answer: I mainly work with Adobe Creative Cloud (Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, After Effects, XD) for graphic design, layout and animation. For 3D visualizations and animations I use Cinema 4D and Blender. On the web I work with HTML, CSS, JavaScript and modern frameworks like React and Next.js. For prototyping and UI/UX design I use Figma and Adobe XD. I'm also familiar with CMS systems like WordPress and Shopware for e-commerce projects. My technical versatility lets me pick the best tools for each project.

lvho8tfe93cioqkayamq8ckq.question: How long does a project take?
lvho8tfe93cioqkayamq8ckq.answer: A logo with stationery takes me two to four weeks; a complete brand identity more like four to eight. Websites and shops including development take six to twelve weeks, depending on the feature set. The biggest time factor is usually you: feedback rounds and finished content decide how fast things move. If it's urgent, say so early – then we'll find a way.

e3a37axaaesk3lxef1ki0vmy.question: How does working together work?
e3a37axaaesk3lxef1ki0vmy.answer: First we talk – about goals, requirements and what matters to you. That turns into a quote. Then I develop first concepts, we discuss them and I refine step by step. You'll see regularly where we stand, with no surprises at the end. Whether remote or on site in Berlin depends on the project – my clients are all over Germany and beyond.

tqso9ujeanib4seth6bzd3ki.question: When can you start?
tqso9ujeanib4seth6bzd3ki.answer: Smaller tasks I can often fit in at short notice alongside ongoing projects; larger ones need some lead time. Whether I'm currently available, you can see from the status in the contact section. Best write to me with a rough time frame, and I'll tell you honestly whether it fits.

nznhd6njk2be0cmhsxgkad0w.question: Do you also work for agencies?
nznhd6njk2be0cmhsxgkad0w.answer: Yes, gladly. I work as a subcontractor for agencies that need design or development capacity. I can plug into existing teams, tools and design systems, or take over a sub-project completely – for example the Shopware implementation of your concept.

pywi5diu4ny5t4hzt6xk1f1q.question: What happens after launch?
pywi5diu4ny5t4hzt6xk1f1q.answer: You're not on your own. After launch I stay available – for small changes, updates or new features. If you prefer things to be predictable, I'll put together an offer for ongoing maintenance; everything else is billed by time and effort. Updates for Shopware, WordPress or plugins I take care of on request, so the shop stays secure.

fafeoerpbz47jkxobweqg5n2.question: What do you own in the end?
fafeoerpbz47jkxobweqg5n2.answer: Everything you need to carry on without me. You receive the usage rights to logo, design and website. Source code and CMS access I hand over after the final payment. Hosting and domain run in your name. What exactly is included is stated in the quote.
